name: screen-simulator-mcp

tools.name: list_browsers
tools.description: List the Chrome browsers/profiles that currently have the Screen Simulator extension connected to this MCP server.

tools.name: list_devices
tools.description: List devices the simulator can emulate: phones, foldables, tablets, laptops, desktop monitors and generic breakpoints. Each has an id (use it in open_simulator/set_devices), CSS viewport size, pixel ratio, platform and touch support.

query.description: Words to match in id, name, brand or size, e.g. "iphone 15" or "1920x1080".

browser.description: Target browser id from list_browsers. Omit to use the most recently active one.

tools.name: open_simulator
tools.description: Open a URL in a new background Chrome tab showing it on one or more devices side by side (realistic frames, real viewport sizes, device user agent, touch emulation). Returns tabId and the device slots. Cookies and logins of the site work because the page runs first-party. Example devices: ["iphone-15-pro","ipad-air-11","macbook-air-13","monitor-1080p"].

devices.description: Device ids from list_devices. Add "@WIDTHxHEIGHT" for a custom viewport with that device's identity ("iphone-15-pro@767x900"), or give just "WIDTHxHEIGHT" ("768x1024") for a plain desktop viewport. Default: the user's default set (phone, tablet, laptop, monitor).

browserUi.description: Subtract browser/status bars from the viewport like a real browser (default true). false = full-screen web app.

sync.description: Sync scrolling and navigation between devices (default true).

accurate.description: Turn on Accurate mode (Chrome debugger: real touch, CSS hover/pointer, pixel ratio). Shows Chrome's yellow debugging bar.

focus.description: Bring the new tab to the front (default false: stays in the background).

browser.description: Target browser id from list_browsers. Omit to use the most recently active one.

tools.name: get_state
tools.description: List the simulator tabs this agent session can control (tabs it opened plus tabs the user shared) with their URL, devices, sizes and modes.

tabId.description: Simulator tab id returned by open_simulator or get_state.

browser.description: Target browser id from list_browsers. Omit to use the most recently active one.

tools.name: set_devices
tools.description: Replace the devices shown in a simulator tab. Pages reload in the new devices.

tabId.description: Simulator tab id returned by open_simulator or get_state.

devices.description: Device ids from list_devices; "id@WIDTHxHEIGHT" or "WIDTHxHEIGHT" for exact viewport sizes (e.g. test 767 vs 768).

browser.description: Target browser id from list_browsers. Omit to use the most recently active one.

tools.name: rotate
tools.description: Rotate a device (or all devices with slot "all") between portrait and landscape.

tabId.description: Simulator tab id returned by open_simulator or get_state.

slot.description: Slot id or "all". Default: focused device.

browser.description: Target browser id from list_browsers. Omit to use the most recently active one.

tools.name: navigate
tools.description: Navigate every device of a simulator tab to a URL and wait until they have loaded.

tabId.description: Simulator tab id returned by open_simulator or get_state.

browser.description: Target browser id from list_browsers. Omit to use the most recently active one.

tools.name: reload
tools.description: Reload a simulator tab and wait until every device has loaded.

tabId.description: Simulator tab id returned by open_simulator or get_state.

browser.description: Target browser id from list_browsers. Omit to use the most recently active one.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Capture device screenshots in the background through the Chrome debugger (a yellow debugging bar may appear briefly). area: "viewport" = what the page shows, "full_page" = the whole scrollable page (100vh sections stay one screen tall; fixed top bars appear once at the top, fixed bottom bars once at the bottom), "with_frame" = device frame included (transparent corners). By default images use CSS pixels (iPhone 15 Pro viewport = 393 px wide), so x/y in the image are the x/y that interact expects; scale "device" gives real device pixels (1179 px wide). No side exceeds maxSide (default 2000); a taller full page comes back as several parts, top to bottom (part, parts, offsetY in CSS px). truncated = the page was longer than the capture limit.

tabId.description: Simulator tab id returned by open_simulator or get_state.

slot.description: Slot id, or "all" (default) for one image per device.

scale.description: "css" (default): 1 image px = 1 CSS px. "device": the device's real pixels.

maxSide.description: Largest width or height of any returned image (default 2000).

browser.description: Target browser id from list_browsers. Omit to use the most recently active one.

tools.name: audit_layout
tools.description: Measure responsive-layout problems in each device: horizontal overflow and the elements causing it, elements outside the viewport, tap targets smaller than 44×44 (iOS) / 48×48 (Android), text under 12px, missing or bad meta viewport, images much larger than displayed, fixed elements covering a large part of the screen, accessibility basics (text below WCAG AA contrast, images without alt, form fields without a label, buttons/links without a name), console errors and failed loads since the page loaded (broken images/scripts, and same-origin requests that returned 4xx/5xx).

tabId.description: Simulator tab id returned by open_simulator or get_state.

browser.description: Target browser id from list_browsers. Omit to use the most recently active one.

tools.name: interact
tools.description: Interact with the page inside one device. tap/click: an element by CSS selector, or x/y in CSS px of the device viewport (= x/y in a default screenshot); the result says covered/coveredBy when something lies on top of the element (a tap then lands on that, as on a real phone). type: fills a field, or picks a <select> option by value or visible text. press: a key ("Enter" submits the form of an input, "Escape", "Tab" moves focus, "ArrowDown", ...). hover: mouse hover events (scripted menus open; CSS :hover does not change). scroll: deltaY/deltaX on the nearest scrollable element at the selector or x/y, else the page; moved=false means nothing scrolled. Taps on touch devices send real touch + pointer events.

tabId.description: Simulator tab id returned by open_simulator or get_state.

slot.description: Device slot ("s1", "s2", …) from open_simulator/get_state. Defaults to the focused device.

text.description: Text to type, or the option to pick in a <select> (action "type").

shift.description: Hold Shift with "press" (Shift+Tab moves focus back).

deltaY.description: Pixels to scroll down (action "scroll"); negative scrolls up.

deltaX.description: Pixels to scroll right (action "scroll"); negative scrolls left.

browser.description: Target browser id from list_browsers. Omit to use the most recently active one.

tools.name: evaluate
tools.description: Run a JavaScript expression in the page of one device, or of every device with slot "all" (then one result per device, e.g. to compare innerWidth or whether the nav is collapsed), and return its JSON-serialisable result (promises are awaited, top-level await works). Runs through the Chrome debugger, so it also works on pages whose CSP forbids eval (a yellow debugging bar may appear briefly). Only works in simulator tabs this agent controls.

tabId.description: Simulator tab id returned by open_simulator or get_state.

slot.description: Slot id, or "all" for every device. Defaults to the focused device.

browser.description: Target browser id from list_browsers. Omit to use the most recently active one.

tools.name: wait_for
tools.description: Wait in one device until an element is visible (or hidden with state "hidden"), a text appears on the page, or the URL contains a string — e.g. after a tap that loads data or navigates. Fails with a clear message after timeout ms (default 10000, max 60000).

tabId.description: Simulator tab id returned by open_simulator or get_state.

slot.description: Device slot ("s1", "s2", …) from open_simulator/get_state. Defaults to the focused device.

state.description: For selector: wait until it is visible (default) or hidden/gone.

text.description: Text that must appear in the page.

url.description: Substring the device URL must contain.

browser.description: Target browser id from list_browsers. Omit to use the most recently active one.

tools.name: set_color_scheme
tools.description: Set the light/dark preference (prefers-color-scheme) of one device or all devices in a simulator tab, so dark mode can be checked side by side with light mode. Pages reload in the affected devices. Applies to matchMedia and to @media rules of stylesheets the page can read (its own origin).

tabId.description: Simulator tab id returned by open_simulator or get_state.

browser.description: Target browser id from list_browsers. Omit to use the most recently active one.

tools.name: set_vision
tools.description: Show one device (or all) the way people with a colour-vision deficiency or blurred vision see it, to check contrast and colour-only cues in screenshots. The page itself is not changed or reloaded; screenshots include the effect.

tabId.description: Simulator tab id returned by open_simulator or get_state.

browser.description: Target browser id from list_browsers. Omit to use the most recently active one.

tools.name: get_logs
tools.description: Console messages (log/info/warn/error/debug) of each device since its page loaded (in tabs this agent opened, or that the user shared: from the device's next load on, since other tabs keep the page's console untouched), plus uncaught errors, broken images/scripts and same-origin requests that returned 4xx/5xx. Pass since (the "now" of an earlier call, ms) to get only new messages, and level to drop quieter ones.

tabId.description: Simulator tab id returned by open_simulator or get_state.

since.description: Only messages at or after this time (ms since epoch), e.g. the "now" returned by the previous call.

browser.description: Target browser id from list_browsers. Omit to use the most recently active one.

tools.name: get_breakpoints
tools.description: List the width breakpoints the page itself uses: every min-width / max-width / range width in its @media rules, including stylesheets from other origins. Use it to pick exact widths to test (e.g. 767 and 768), then set_devices with "WIDTHxHEIGHT".

tabId.description: Simulator tab id returned by open_simulator or get_state.

slot.description: Device slot ("s1", "s2", …) from open_simulator/get_state. Defaults to the focused device.

browser.description: Target browser id from list_browsers. Omit to use the most recently active one.

tools.name: set_reduced_motion
tools.description: Turn prefers-reduced-motion: reduce on or off for one device or all devices, to check that animations and parallax calm down for users who ask for less motion. Pages reload in the affected devices. Applies to matchMedia and to @media rules of the page's stylesheets.

tabId.description: Simulator tab id returned by open_simulator or get_state.

reduce.description: true = the device asks for reduced motion.

browser.description: Target browser id from list_browsers. Omit to use the most recently active one.

tools.name: set_accurate_mode
tools.description: Turn Accurate mode on/off for a simulator tab and set throttling. Accurate mode uses the Chrome debugger so CSS hover/pointer queries, pixel ratio, client hints and touch are exact for the focused device; Chrome shows a yellow debugging bar while it is on.

tabId.description: Simulator tab id returned by open_simulator or get_state.

browser.description: Target browser id from list_browsers. Omit to use the most recently active one.

tools.name: close_simulator
tools.description: Close a simulator. Tabs this agent opened are closed; tabs the user shared are returned to normal.

tabId.description: Simulator tab id returned by open_simulator or get_state.

browser.description: Target browser id from list_browsers. Omit to use the most recently active one.

instructions:
Screen Simulator shows web pages on real device sizes inside the user's Chrome.
Typical flow: open_simulator({url, devices}) → screenshot({tabId}) and audit_layout({tabId}) → fix the code → reload({tabId}) → check again → close_simulator.
Use list_devices to pick ids (phones, tablets, laptops, desktop monitors, breakpoints), or "id@WIDTHxHEIGHT" / "WIDTHxHEIGHT" for exact widths; get_breakpoints lists the page's own.
Screenshots use CSS pixels by default (image x/y = interact x/y); scale "device" gives real device pixels. Long full pages come back in parts.
After a tap that loads something, use wait_for instead of sleeping; get_logs shows console output and failed loads.
Rendering is Chrome's (Blink) even for iPhone devices, so Safari-only engine bugs cannot be reproduced.
